end.summary:
Named liquid, solid ice and invisible water vapour, with places they are found; practised through easy questions, with a why or new-situation check still needed.
Practised that most Earth water is salty and fresh water is a tiny part; this is still building.
Practised evaporation, condensation, freezing and melting; some examples were right, but the idea that water does not disappear needs checking next time.
The belief that cold-glass drops leak through the glass was not corrected in this lesson.
end.parentNote: Sana practised the three forms of water and connected them with rivers, seas, glaciers, freezers and air. They used the idea that water can move into invisible vapour, but later mixed this up by saying the water was gone, and the cold-glass drops were still explained as leaking through the glass. At home, try observing a drying cloth and drops forming on a cold glass, then ask where each water drop came from and where the drying water went.
